Differentiation: Composite, Implicit, and Inverse Functions
UNIT
3
AP Calculus AB and BC · Course Framework return to ContenTS 75
TOPIC3.6
Calculating Higher -
Order Derivatives
LEARNINGOBJECTIVE
FUN-3.F
Determine higher order
derivatives of a function.
ESSENTIALKNOWLEDGE
FUN-3.F.1
Differentiating f ′produces the second
derivative f ″, provided the derivative of f ′
exists; repeating this process produces higher-
order derivatives of f.
FUN-3.F.2
Higher-order derivatives are represented with a
variety of notations. For y = f(x), notations for
the second derivative include
d y 2
dx2
, , f″(x) and
y″. Higher-order derivatives can be denoted
d y n
dxn
or f(n)
(x).
ENDURINGUNDERSTANDING
FUN-3
Recognizing opportunities to apply derivative rules can simplify differentiation.
SUGGESTEDSKILLS
Implementing
Mathematical Processes
1.E
Apply appropriate
mathematical rules or
procedures, with and without
technology.
